metaDesc: Where to go for temples and sacred sites in Thailand? Six picks — Ayutthaya, Sukhothai, Chiang Mai, Nan, Nakhon Phanom and Nakhon Si Thammarat — with where to stay.
ogTitle: Best Temple Destinations in Thailand 2026 — 6 Sacred Picks
ogDesc: Provinces with beautiful temples and revered stupas, ideal for temple-lovers and fans of ancient architecture, each with where to stay.
intro: Provinces with beautiful temples and revered stupas, ideal for temple-lovers and fans of ancient architecture, each with where to stay.

blocks.html: Short answer: For ancient ruins choose Ayutthaya and Sukhothai; for Lanna temples, Chiang Mai (Doi Suthep) or Nan (Wat Phumin); for revered stupas, Nakhon Phanom (Phra That Phanom) and Nakhon Si Thammarat (Wat Phra Mahathat).

items.name: Ayutthaya
items.blurb: A World Heritage city full of old temples and stupas — highlights include the Buddha head in the tree roots at Wat Mahathat and riverside Wat Chaiwatthanaram at dusk.

items.name: Sukhothai
items.blurb: The historical park of Thailand’s first capital — Wat Mahathat and the giant Buddha face at Wat Si Chum, with a full day of cycling among ruins and lotus ponds.

items.name: Chiang Mai
items.blurb: Lanna temples inside the old moat plus Wat Phra That Doi Suthep on its hilltop with city views — the signature temple every Chiang Mai visitor climbs up to.

items.name: Nan
items.blurb: Wat Phumin with its “whispering lovers” mural and the quiet old temples of Nan town — a small-town setting that is lovely for a temple stroll.

items.name: Nakhon Phanom
items.blurb: Phra That Phanom, a sacred stupa central to the Mekong and Isan people, in a quiet riverside town with Laos across the water — a key pilgrimage for merit-makers.

items.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat
items.blurb: Wat Phra Mahathat, the South’s great golden stupa, plus the Ai Khai shrine at Wat Chedi that draws merit-seekers hoping for good fortune.

faq.q: Which province is best for merit-making?
faq.a: Nakhon Phanom (Phra That Phanom) and Nakhon Si Thammarat (Wat Phra Mahathat and the Ai Khai shrine) are favorites for merit-making and birth-year stupa pilgrimages, while Chiang Mai’s Doi Suthep is a sacred temple visited by Thais and foreigners alike.

faq.q: Ayutthaya or Sukhothai for ancient ruins?
faq.a: Ayutthaya is near Bangkok and doable as a day trip, with large ruins spread across town, while Sukhothai is farther but has a tidy, scenic park that is easy to cycle and feels calmer — choose by your time and how far you want to travel.

faq.q: What should I wear to temples?
faq.a: Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, for both men and women; some temples lend cover-ups. Remove your shoes before entering the ordination or assembly hall, keep your voice down and do not point your feet at Buddha images.
